title: Compact Stars
description: Neutron stars, magnetars, pulsars and quark stars - the densest objects short of a singularity.

puzzle.goal: A neutron star with moment of inertia I spins at angular velocity Ω. Its magnetic dipole m, tilted by α from the rotation axis, radiates electromagnetic waves like a rotating antenna, and that radiated power is drawn from the rotational kinetic energy. Write the rate of change of that energy.
puzzle.name: Magnetic-dipole spin-down of a pulsar
puzzle.ask: Since dΩ/dt ∝ −Ω³, integrating from a fast birth spin gives the characteristic age τ = P/(2Ṗ). Find it in years for the Crab pulsar (1 yr = 31 557 600 s).

vars.\u03b1: angle between magnetic and spin axes

puzzle.method: A rotating dipole has a second time derivative of size mΩ² sin α; insert it into the power radiated by an accelerated dipole, and set the result equal to minus the change of rotational energy.
